description.en-US: The stable identifier a human or an import file names this pricelist by. Immutable and unique across the tenant, because a pricelist is referenced from spreadsheets and integration payloads that nobody will update if it is renamed.

What commercial policy this list represents, in the words of whoever set it up. Free text: the code identifies the list and the name labels it, but neither has room to say why a wholesale list exists or who negotiated it.

The currency every price on this list is quoted in (BR-PRICE-CUR-001). Required, and one per list: a list holding some prices in VND and others in USD could not be compared against an order's currency without knowing which row meant which, and there is no FX service to reconcile them (BR-PRICE-CUR-004).

A list carries its own currency rather than inheriting the organization's, because a USD export list is exactly the case this exists for. That is also why changing it after the fact is refused once the list has rules or has priced a transaction: reinterpreting 100 USD as 100 VND is the failure the requirement names. Create a new list instead.

A plain ulid with no edge — currency belongs to Essential, and a foreign key across a module boundary would make Sales' schema depend on Essential's table.

Whether an order that names no pricelist falls back to this one. At most one non-archived default per organization (BR-PRICE-SAL-003), which the domain service enforces — the schema cannot express uniqueness conditional on is_archived.

Distinct from the scope columns above and not a substitute for them: a default answers "which list when none was chosen", while channel and point answer "which list applies here". A global list is not automatically the default, and the default need not be global.

Setting it is its own operation rather than an ordinary update, because promoting one list must demote the other in the same breath; two updates would leave a window with two defaults or none.

The channel this pricelist applies to, or NULL for one that applies everywhere. Nullability IS the specificity mechanism: resolution prefers a sales-point list over a channel list over a global one, so leaving both scope columns NULL is how a default price list is expressed rather than a missing value.

The single selling place this pricelist applies to, or NULL. The most specific scope: an airport kiosk charging more than the same chain's high street store is a point-scoped list, and it wins over its channel's.

When this pricelist starts applying, or NULL for always. Effective dating rather than editing in place: a price change scheduled for next month must not alter what today's sales are charged, and a pricelist whose window has closed is still needed to explain the orders priced under it.

When it stops applying, or NULL for open-ended. Exclusive of the instant itself, matching every other window in this module, so that one list ending and the next beginning at the same moment leaves no gap and no overlap.

Breaks ties between two pricelists of the SAME specificity, higher winning. It does not override specificity: a point-scoped list beats a channel-scoped one whatever their priorities, because otherwise a high-priority global list would silently undo every local price.
